mainTopic: Wordings for קידושין and גירושין, and giving them without explaining (רבי יוסי)
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining שמואל: wordings where the man speaks about himself, like 'I am your husband', do nothing, because the פסוק says he takes her and sends her, not himself. A ברייתא lists six phrases that work for קידושין, and the גמרא explains that they are split into two groups only because that is how the תנא learned them. Next the חכמים ask about ten unclear phrases. 'לקוחתי' works because of 'כי יקח'. 'חרופה' works in יהודה, where people use that word for a betrothed woman. The גמרא shows the question must be about a couple already discussing קידושין, where he gave money and also said one of the phrases. The doubt is whether he meant קידושין or was hiring her for work, and it ends in תיקו. The גמרא then studies the משנה of רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה about giving without explaining. The rule needs the couple to still be on the topic, or at least on a related point (אביי), and the הלכה follows רבי יוסי. Someone who does not know this rule should not rule on גיטין and קידושין. Finally the גמרא lists phrases that work for divorce and begins a case of 'you are a free woman', which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: שמואל's real point is about the last set of wordings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers why שמואל needed to speak. His new teaching is about the later wordings, where the man speaks about himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The last expressions are what he is teaching us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question it was just asking: what new thing does שמואל teach? It says the new point is in the last group of wordings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל listed wordings like 'I am your husband' for קידושין and 'I am not your husband' for גירושין. The point is that these man-centered wordings do nothing at all. There is not even a doubt that they work. The next step gives the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: the last ones, the later ones
this is what he teaches us (the new point)

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a discussion from the previous עמוד. The 'last expressions' are שמואל's wordings where the man speaks about himself, like 'I am your husband'.

phrases.english: The last expressions are what he teaches us:
phrases.notes: He means the wordings that talk about the man himself, like 'I am your husband' or 'I am not your husband'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from before this section about what שמואל's statement adds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies which part of the statement holds the new teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think שמואל's statement teaches nothing new.
steps.terutzMaskana: The new teaching is that wordings about the man himself have no effect at all.

steps.title: The man acts on the woman, not on himself
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'כי יקח' and 'ושלחה'. The man takes her and sends her away. He does not take or send himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it says 'when he takes', not that he takes himself. And here it says 'and he sends her', not that he sends himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for why wordings about the man himself do not work. It uses two words from the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In קידושין the man must act on the woman ('takes'). Saying 'I am your husband' puts the action on himself. The same is true of גירושין: 'he sends her', so 'I am not your husband' does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: when [a man] takes, the source for קידושין
and he sends her away, the source for גירושין

steps.whatToRemember: In both קידושין and גירושין the man must act on the woman. Wordings that put the action on himself have no effect.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic rule: the wording must place the act of acquiring or sending away on the woman.

phrases.english: Here it is written: 'When he takes'
and not that he takes himself.
And here it is written: 'And he sends her'
and not that he sends himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the point made in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That man-centered wordings have no effect for קידושין or גירושין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words 'כי יקח' and 'ושלחה' in דברים 24:1

steps.title: A ברייתא lists six phrases that create קידושין
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives two groups of three phrases. In each group, if he says the phrase, she is מקודשת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'You are my wife', 'my betrothed', 'acquired to me': she is מקודשת. 'You are mine', 'in my domain', 'bound to me': she is מקודשת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a ברייתא, listing six wordings that work for קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All six phrases are said to the woman and describe her as belonging to him, which fits the rule from step 2. The ברייתא splits them into two groups, each ending with 'מקודשת'. This split leads to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: in my domain, under my authority

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
'You are hereby my wife,'
'You are hereby my betrothed,'
'You are hereby acquired to me': she is betrothed.
'You are hereby mine,'
'You are hereby under my authority,'
'You are hereby bound to me': she is betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: which phrases are valid for קידושין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of these six phrases, said to the woman, creates קידושין.

steps.title: Why not list all six together?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא splits the phrases into two groups when the ruling is the same for all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it teach them all together!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the way the ברייתא is written. Since every phrase gives the same result, why say 'מקודשת' twice?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Splitting a list usually hints that the groups differ in law. Here both groups end the same way, so the split looks unnecessary.

phrases.english: But let it teach them all together!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the structure of the ברייתא from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two-group form of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling is the same for both groups, so dividing them seems pointless.

steps.title: The תנא kept the form he learned
steps.stepSummary: The תנא heard the phrases as two groups of three and taught them exactly as he heard them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא heard them three and three, and taught them that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the split has no legal meaning. It just reflects how the material was passed down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two groups are not different in law. The תנא received them as two separate teachings of three, and kept that form out of faithfulness to his teachers.

keyTerms.meaning: three and three, two groups of three

phrases.english: The tanna heard them three by three,
he heard them and taught them that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording as following how it was passed down, not a difference in law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The split might hint at a legal difference between the two groups.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no difference. The split only reflects how the תנא received the teaching.
steps.whatToRemember: All six phrases in the ברייתא work for קידושין. The two groups are only about how the teaching was passed down.

steps.title: Ten unclear phrases: do they work?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask about ten phrases whose meaning for קידושין is unclear, such as 'unique to me', 'my helper' and 'my rib'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: 'unique to me', 'designated to me', 'my helper', 'my counterpart', 'my gathered one', 'my rib', 'my closed one', 'beneath me', 'my seized one', 'my taken one': what is the law for each?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is raised. Do these less clear wordings create קידושין?
steps.deeperAnalysis: These phrases are vaguer than the ones in the ברייתא. Some may hint at marriage, like 'my rib' or 'my helper', but they could also mean something else. So it is unclear whether they show a clear intent to acquire her as a wife.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was raised before them

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
'Unique to me': what is the law?
'Designated to me': what is the law?
'My helper': what is the law? 'My counterpart': what is the law?
'My gathered one': what is the law? 'My rib': what is the law?
'My closed one': what is the law? 'Beneath me': what is the law?
'My seized one': what is the law? 'My taken one': what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the clearly valid phrases, the גמרא turns to unclear ones.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether each of these ten vaguer phrases creates קידושין

steps.title: 'My taken one' works, based on 'כי יקח'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles one of the ten from a ברייתא: 'לקוחתי' creates קידושין, because the פסוק calls קידושין 'taking'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Resolve at least one, as a ברייתא teaches: one who says 'my taken one', she is מקודשת, because it says 'when a man takes a woman'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers one part of the question using a ברייתא. The other phrases come back in steps 14–17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לקוחתי' comes from the same root as 'יקח', the very word the תורה uses for קידושין. So this wording clearly matches the תורה's language and works.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is taught in a ברייתא
as it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: 'לקוחתי' creates קידושין because it uses the תורה's own word for marriage, 'כי יקח'.

phrases.english: Resolve at least one,
as it is taught: one who says 'my taken one'
she is betrothed,
because it is stated: 'When a man takes a woman.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the last item in the question from step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לקוחתי' creates קידושין, based on a ברייתא that uses the פסוק 'כי יקח איש אשה'.

steps.title: What about saying 'my espoused one'?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask whether saying ״חרופתי״ creates קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if he says ״חרופתי״, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about another one of the unclear phrases: ״חרופתי״, 'my espoused one'. This question sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״חרופה״ is not an everyday word for a betrothed woman. So it is unclear whether a woman hearing it would understand that he means קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the חכמים

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
If he says 'my espoused one', what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from ״לקוחתי״ to another phrase whose meaning for קידושין is unclear.

steps.title: A ברייתא says 'my espoused one' works
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that ״חרופתי״ creates קידושין, because in יהודה a betrothed woman is called ״חרופה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as a ברייתא teaches: one who says ״חרופתי״, she is מקודשת, because in יהודה they call a betrothed woman ״חרופה״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question: ״חרופתי״ works. The reason given is how people speak in יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's reason is about how people speak, not a פסוק. Since people in יהודה use ״חרופה״ to mean a betrothed woman, the phrase clearly means קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a proof is coming)
The region of יהודה in ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught in a ברייתא:
One who says 'my espoused one', she is betrothed,
because in יהודה they call a betrothed woman 'charufa'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 from a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״חרופתי״ creates קידושין, based on the way people speak in יהודה.

steps.title: Is יהודה the whole world?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: why should a rule for everyone depend on how people talk in יהודה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And is יהודה most of the world?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's reason. The way people talk in one region should not set the law for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sounded like a general rule: whoever says ״חרופתי״ is מקודש. But its reason only applies in יהודה. The גמרא points out that this reason is too local to support a rule for everyone.

phrases.english: And is יהודה most of the world?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in the ברייתא of step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reason, which depends on how people talk in יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A local way of speaking cannot be the basis for a rule that applies everywhere.

steps.title: The real source is a פסוק, and יהודה is extra support
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is reread: ״חרופתי״ works because of a פסוק, and the way people talk in יהודה is only an added point.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: one who says ״חרופתי״, she is מקודשת, as it says 'and she is a maidservant espoused to a man'. And furthermore, in יהודה they call a betrothed woman ״חרופה״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the main source is a פסוק that uses the word ״נחרפת״ for a betrothed woman. The way people talk in יהודה is just extra support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a פסוק uses this word for a betrothed woman, the rule applies everywhere. That answers the objection that יהודה is not the whole world. The point about יהודה becomes only a secondary ״ועוד״ (and furthermore).

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (rereading a source)

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
One who says 'my espoused one', she is betrothed,
as it is stated: 'And she is a maidservant espoused to a man.'
And furthermore, in יהודה they call a betrothed woman 'charufa'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the ברייתא against the objection of step 10 by rereading it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא to add a hidden source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא relies only on how people talk in יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא relies on a פסוק, and יהודה is only extra support.

steps.title: Why add a local custom to a פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: once there is a פסוק, adding the way people talk in יהודה as ״ועוד״ makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: And would one add יהודה with 'furthermore' to a פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reading of step 11. A פסוק is much stronger proof than local speech, so the extra point adds nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ״ועוד״ is used to add support to an argument. But a פסוק is already full proof, and how people talk in one region is far weaker. Adding the weaker point to the stronger one does not fit.

phrases.english: And would יהודה be added with 'furthermore' to a verse?
phrases.notes: He means: once you have a פסוק, why bother adding how people talk in one region?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rereading offered in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the ברייתא gives a פסוק and then adds יהודה as ״ועוד״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A weak local proof does not get added as ״ועוד״ to a פסוק, which is already full proof.

steps.title: The rule applies only in יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is finally explained as a local rule: saying ״חרופה״ creates קידושין in יהודה, where people speak that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what it means: one who says ״חרופה״ in יהודה, she is מקודשת, because in יהודה they call a betrothed woman ״חרופה״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the פסוק reading. It explains that the ברייתא was only ever talking about someone who says this in יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'is יהודה the whole world?' no longer applies, because the ברייתא never meant to make a rule for everyone. The law follows how people speak where the words are said.
steps.whatToRemember: ״חרופה״ creates קידושין in a place where people use that word for a betrothed woman, such as יהודה.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it is saying:
One who says 'espoused' in יהודה, she is betrothed,
because in יהודה they call a betrothed woman 'charufa'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading of step 11 with a new reading that also answers step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ruling to one place
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא gives a rule for everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's rule is only for יהודה, where people speak this way.

steps.title: If they weren't discussing קידושין, how would she understand?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case all these phrases are about. If the couple was not discussing קידושין, she could not know what he means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If we say he was not speaking with her about her גט or her קידושין, how does she know what he is saying to her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a broad question about all the unclear phrases: what situation are they talking about? This step looks at the first option and shows it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without any discussion of marriage beforehand, an unclear phrase could mean many things. She would have no way to know he means קידושין. So the question cannot be about that case.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
Matters of her גט and her קידושין

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not only about ״חרופה״. It goes back to all the unclear phrases the חכמים asked about.

phrases.english: With what case are we dealing?
phrases.notes: This asks about all the unclear phrases from the list of ten, not just this last one.

phrases.english: If we say where he was not speaking with her
about matters of her divorce document and her betrothal,
from where does she know what he is saying to her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ״חרופה״ discussion and questions the basic case behind all the unclear phrases.
steps.kashyaTarget: The question about the ten unclear phrases (step 6)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: First option: with no earlier discussion of marriage, an unclear phrase cannot tell her he means קידושין.

steps.title: If they were discussing קידושין, no words are needed at all
steps.stepSummary: If they were discussing קידושין, a משנה and the הלכה like רבי יוסי show that she is מקודשת even if he says nothing. So what is the question about?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he was speaking with her about her גט and her קידושין, then even if he said nothing she is also מקודשת. As the משנה teaches: if he was speaking with a woman about her גט and her קידושין, and he gave her the גט or the קידושין without explaining, רבי יוסי says it is enough, and רבי יהודה says he must explain. And רב הונא said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at the second option and shows it also fails. When the topic is already being discussed, giving the money is enough even without words, so these phrases do not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows that, according to רבי יוסי, the earlier conversation makes his intent clear on its own. Since the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, no phrase is needed. Both options now seem to leave nothing to ask. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up an important principle: the conversation before giving קידושין can make his intent clear, even without words.

phrases.english: But rather, where he was speaking with her
about matters of her divorce document and her betrothal,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אָמַר לָהּ נָמֵי,
phrases.english: even though he did not say anything to her, she is also betrothed,
as we learned in a משנה: If he was speaking with a woman
about matters of her divorce document and her betrothal,

phrases.aramaic: וְנָתַן לָהּ גִּיטָּהּ וְקִידּוּשֶׁיהָ וְלֹא פֵּירֵשׁ –
phrases.english: and he gave her the divorce document or her betrothal, but did not explain,
רבי יוסי says: It is enough.
רבי יהודה says: He must explain.
And רב הונא said that שמואל said:
The law follows רבי יוסי!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא בִּמְדַבֵּר עִמָּהּ עַל עִסְקֵי גִּיטָּהּ וְקִידּוּשֶׁיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided challenge of step 14 by showing that the second option fails too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The question about the ten unclear phrases (step 6)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Second option: if they were discussing קידושין, the הלכה like רבי יוסי makes words unnecessary, so the exact phrase should not matter.

steps.title: The case: they were discussing קידושין, and he gave money while saying one of the phrases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: the couple was talking about קידושין. If he had stayed silent, she would be מקודשת. The question is about a case where he gave her money and also said one of these phrases.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: Really, we are talking about a case where he was speaking with her about her divorce or her קידושין. And it is true that if he had given her money and stayed quiet, she would be מקודשת. Our case is different: he gave her the money and also said one of these phrases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from steps 14–15 by explaining exactly which case the question is about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 asked: if they were discussing קידושין, then silence already works, so what is there to ask? The answer is that the phrase he added is the new factor. Saying something may actually raise a doubt that silence would not have raised.

keyTerms.meaning: They say. This introduces an answer from the Sages.
Really, actually. The original assumption stays in place.
Matters of her divorce or her betrothal

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume that saying more always makes things clearer. In this case, his extra words are exactly what might create the doubt.

phrases.english: They say: Really, it is where he was speaking with her
about matters of her divorce and her betrothal,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי דְּיָהֵיב לַהּ וְשָׁתֵיק הָכִי נָמֵי,
phrases.english: and if he gave her and stayed silent, so it is indeed (she is betrothed),
phrases.notes: This admits the point from step 15: silence while talking about קידושין already works.

phrases.english: here, what are we dealing with?

phrases.aramaic: דִּיהַב לַהּ וַאֲמַר לַהּ בְּהָנֵי לִישָּׁנֵי,
phrases.english: Where he gave her and said to her one of these expressions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 by identifying the exact case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question seemed pointless: without discussion she can't understand him, and with discussion silence already works.
steps.terutzMaskana: They were discussing קידושין, and he said a phrase while giving. The phrase itself may create a doubt.

steps.title: Was the phrase about קידושין or about hiring her for work? Unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The real question is whether these phrases mean קידושין or mean he is paying her for work. The גמרא leaves it unresolved: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what was being asked: when he said these phrases, did he mean them for קידושין? Or maybe he meant them for work, as payment to hire her? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the question clearly and then leaves it unanswered with תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Phrases like ״עזרתי״ or ״תחתי״ could describe a wife, but they could also describe a worker or servant. By saying them, he may have switched away from the קידושין they were discussing. No proof is found for these phrases either way.

keyTerms.meaning: He is asking, this is his question
Let it stand. The question remains unresolved.

steps.whatToRemember: These phrases are a doubt: they might mean קידושין, or they might mean he is hiring her. The question stays open (תיקו).
steps.whyThisMatters: Since it is a תיקו, a woman betrothed with one of these phrases is in a doubtful status. In practice this is treated as ספק קידושין.

phrases.english: And this is what he is asking:
These expressions, did he say them to her for betrothal,
or perhaps he said them to her for work?
phrases.notes: He means the money might be wages for hiring her, not קידושין money.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the question that step 16's case creates, then closes it as unresolved.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do these phrases point to קידושין, or to hiring her for labor?
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: תיקו: the question is left unresolved.

steps.title: The משנה itself: giving קידושין or a גט without explaining
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה it quoted earlier. If they were discussing divorce or קידושין and he gave without explaining, רבי יוסי says that is enough, and רבי יהודה says he must explain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now the teaching itself: If he was talking with a woman about her divorce or her קידושין, and he gave her a גט or קידושין and did not explain, רבי יוסי says that is enough. רבי יהודה says he must explain.
steps.whatsHappening: With the word גופא, the גמרא goes back to study the משנה (quoted in step 15) on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that the surrounding conversation explains what the giving means. רבי יהודה holds that he must say it out loud. Step 15 already noted that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself. The גמרא returns to study a source it quoted earlier.

phrases.english: The matter itself: If he was speaking with the woman
about matters of her divorce or her betrothal,

phrases.aramaic: וְנָתַן לָהּ גִּיטָּהּ וְקִידּוּשֶׁיהָ וְלֹא פֵּירֵשׁ –
phrases.english: and he gave her her גט or her betrothal and did not explain,
Rabbi Yosei says: It is enough.
Rabbi Yehuda says: He must explain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה cited in step 15 and examines it directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: giving during the conversation is enough, with no words needed. רבי יהודה: he must explain.

steps.title: Two אמוראים add a condition: they must still be on that topic
steps.stepSummary: שמואל (quoted by רב יהודה) and רבי אושעיא (quoted by רבי אלעזר) both say the rule only works if they are still talking about that subject when he gives.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: This is only when they are still busy with that topic. And likewise, רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא: This is only when they are still busy with that topic.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים limit רבי יוסי's rule. The conversation explains the giving only if it is still going on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If they had already moved on to a different subject, the earlier talk no longer explains what the money is for. Two separate chains of אמוראים give the same condition, which shows it is widely held.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is only when, provided that
Still busy with that same topic
And likewise said. Another אמורא says the same thing.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
And this is only when they are busy with that same topic.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: And likewise Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Oshaya said:
And this is only when they are busy with that same topic.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: וְהוּא שֶׁעֲסוּקִין בְּאוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limiting condition to רבי יוסי's ruling in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Giving without words works only while they are still discussing that subject.

steps.title: The same condition is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that this condition matches a dispute between תנאים. רבי requires that they still be on the topic. רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון says it works even if they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים. רבי says: This is only when they are busy with that same topic. רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון says: Even if they are not busy with that same topic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the condition of the אמוראים to an earlier dispute between תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי agrees with שמואל and רבי אושעיא. רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון holds that the earlier conversation is enough to explain the giving, even after they changed the subject. So the condition from step 19 is one side of a real dispute among תנאים.
steps.whatToRemember: Under רבי יוסי, giving without words works when they were talking about קידושין or a גט. שמואל, רבי אושעיא and רבי add that they must still be on that topic. רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון does not require this.

phrases.english: It is like a dispute between תנאים:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: וְהוּא שֶׁעֲסוּקִין בְּאוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן.
phrases.english: Rabbi says: And this is only when they are busy with that same topic.
phrases.notes: When the גמרא just says רבי, it means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין עֲסוּקִין בְּאוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן.
phrases.english: Even though they are not busy with that same topic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the condition from step 19 is already the subject of a dispute between תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: they must still be on the topic. רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון: it works even if they are not.

steps.title: How would she understand him if the topic had changed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון: if they are no longer on the topic, she cannot know what his giving means.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they were not still talking about that subject, how would she know what he is saying to her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the view of רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון from the last step. He said the giving works even if they are no longer on the topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving without explaining only works because the conversation makes the meaning clear. If the conversation has moved on, nothing tells her this is קידושין or a גט. So the גמרא asks how his view can make sense.

phrases.english: And if they were not discussing that same subject,
from where does she know what he is saying to her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the opinion of רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון brought in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון's view that the giving works even if they are no longer on the topic.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without the conversation, the woman has no way to understand what the unexplained giving means.

steps.title: They moved to a side-topic of the same subject
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that they moved to a related point while still inside the same general subject.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They moved from one point to another point, but still within the same general subject.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון. The couple did not switch to something totally different. They moved to a related detail of the same subject.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the case is narrower: they stopped talking about the קידושין or divorce itself, but they are still on related matters. That background is enough for her to understand him. So רבי's view needs the exact topic, and רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון is happy with the wider subject.

keyTerms.meaning: from one topic to another topic

phrases.english: Abaye said:
From one topic to another topic, within that same subject.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case: the topic changed only partly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון meant they had moved to a completely different subject, which would leave her with no way to understand.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are on a related side-topic of the same subject, so his meaning is still clear to her.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא in the name of שמואל rules like רבי יוסי: giving without explaining works when they were discussing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא gives a practical ruling on the מחלוקת from step 18. We follow רבי יוסי, not רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי said that if they were discussing קידושין or divorce and he gave without explaining, it works. רבי יהודה said he must say it out loud. שמואל rules like רבי יוסי, so the context of the conversation is enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: This makes the case of giving without words a real working rule in הלכה, not just a theory.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי from step 18, who said giving without explaining is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה of step 18 and decides between רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If they were discussing קידושין or divorce and he gave without explaining, it is valid, like רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Is someone who missed this ruling unfit to handle גיטין and קידושין?
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר asks רב אשי whether שמואל's rule about knowing גיטין and קידושין applies even to someone who did not hear this ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר said to רב אשי: שמואל also said that anyone who does not know the details of גיטין and קידושין should not deal with them. Does that apply even to someone who just never heard this ruling of רב הונא in the name of שמואל?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר brings another statement of שמואל and asks how far it goes. He wants to know if missing this one rule makes a person unfit to rule on these cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said only experts in גיטין and קידושין should rule on them. This rule about giving without words is a less common case. So רב יימר asks: does not knowing just this detail really make someone count as a non-expert?

keyTerms.meaning: the nature and details of divorce documents and קידושין

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יֵימַר לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Yeimar said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: But then, that which Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ בְּטִיב גִּיטִּין וְקִידּוּשִׁין
phrases.english: Anyone who does not know the nature of bills of divorce and betrothals
should have no dealings with them,
phrases.notes: He means he should not act as a judge or rule on these cases.

phrases.english: does that apply even if he did not hear
this ruling that Rav Huna said in the name of Shmuel?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ לָא שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ הָא דְּרַב הוּנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the importance of the ruling just given in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether not knowing this specific ruling makes a person count as someone who does not know the details of גיטין and קידושין.

steps.title: Yes, he is unfit
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that yes, someone who does not know this ruling should not deal with גיטין and קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes, that is indeed so.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question in one short line: yes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling counts as a basic part of the laws of קידושין and divorce. A judge who does not know it could rule wrongly, for example by saying a married woman is not married. So he does not have the needed knowledge.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה is like רבי יוסי: giving without explaining works if they were discussing it. This rule is important enough that someone who does not know it should not rule on גיטין and קידושין.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes, it is indeed so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יימר's question in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. Not knowing this ruling makes a person unfit to deal with גיטין and קידושין.

steps.title: Phrases that work for divorce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to שמואל's earlier statement and brings its divorce half: if he gives a גט and says one of three phrases, she is divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same is true for divorce: if he gave her a גט and said to her, 'You are sent away,' or 'You are divorced,' or 'You are permitted to any man,' she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to שמואל's statement from the previous עמוד about which phrases work for קידושין. Now it brings the matching part about divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as certain phrases work with money for קידושין, certain phrases work with a גט for divorce. Each of these three phrases clearly means the marriage is ending. So when said along with giving the גט, she is divorced.

phrases.english: And similarly with divorce:
phrases.notes: This continues שמואל's statement from the previous עמוד about phrases for קידושין.

phrases.english: If he gave her her bill of divorce and said to her:
"You are hereby sent away,"
"You are hereby divorced,"
"You are hereby permitted to any man"
then she is divorced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יוסי discussion and goes back to the second half of שמואל's statement about phrases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Giving a גט with 'you are sent away', 'you are divorced', or 'you are permitted to any man' makes her divorced.

steps.title: Starting an obvious case: 'You are a free woman'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to say something is obvious: a man gave his wife a גט and said 'You are a free woman'. The sentence continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious: if he gave her a גט and said to his wife, 'You are a free woman'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It starts with 'פשיטא' (it is obvious) and describes a case, but the ruling comes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'You are a free woman' is the phrase used to free a שפחה, not to divorce a wife. The גמרא is about to point out how obvious this case is, and then go on to the case that really needs discussing.

keyTerms.meaning: a free woman, the language used to free a שפחה

steps.confusionAlert: This sentence is not finished here. Do not guess the ruling yet; the גמרא gives it in the next lines.

phrases.english: It is obvious:

phrases.aramaic: נָתַן לָהּ גִּיטָּהּ, וְאָמַר לָהּ לְאִשְׁתּוֹ:
phrases.english: if he gave her a bill of divorce and said to his wife:
"You are hereby a free woman"
phrases.notes: These are the words used to free a שפחה. The ruling comes right after this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts discussing which phrases work for divorce, building on שמואל's list in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces an obvious case of a wife told 'you are a free woman'. The ruling continues on the next עמוד.
